description: A second amplitude buffer for Adje: it turns one CV into a polyphonic one with a different delay for each partial, and it goes immediately to the right of an Adje

params.text: Sets how long the CV takes to travel from one partial to the next, up to 4 seconds; fully clockwise it freezes the buffer
Draws fresh delays, and with the menu option on it also empties the buffer

inputs.text: A reading above 2.5V draws fresh delays, and with the menu option on it also empties the buffer
The CV recorded into the buffer; with nothing patched here the buffer is switched off and the output stops moving
Adds to the delay knob, a volt covering a tenth of its travel
Steps the buffer on each reading above 2.5V, which turns the delay knob into a clock divider rather than a time

outputs.text: The buffered CV, one channel per partial, matching the channel count of the Adje to the left

notes: with no Adje immediately to the left the module falls back to a fixed sixteen channels; a red arrow mark at the top left is what says a parent was found
a Bufke can also follow another Bufke to its left, so several of them can be chained from one Adje
a reset or a randomise on the parent Adje resets this module at the same moment
the module stops while its output is unpatched
menu: CV buffer order: Low→high, High→low, Random — sets the order the CV travels through the partials
Empty buffer on reset — clears the buffer on a reset instead of leaving what is already in it
Follow left module: Free, Sync clock, Get delay time — takes the clock, or the exact delay time, from the module to the left instead of from this panel

inputs.0:
high above 2.5V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads nothing recorded, the buffer switched off.
inputs.2:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
inputs.3:
high above 2.5V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads unclocked, the delay read as a time; a negative voltage does nothing here.
